questions.question: Which field is the load-bearing one in a handoff packet?
options: commands_run, since the next session cannot start without a full command history
summary, since every other field in the packet is derived from that one paragraph
next_action; without it the document is a status report, not a handoff
verdict_pointer, since the next session cannot trust a packet without a verdict link
questions.explanation: A handoff with everything except next_action is a status report; the next concrete step is what makes the next session productive.

questions.question: Why are handoffs generated, not written?
options: Hand-written handoffs get skipped on a hard day; the generator reads workbench artifacts instead
Generated handoffs compress to a much smaller file size than an equivalent hand-written packet ever could
Generated handoffs are the only format the next session's loader is able to parse at all
Hand-written handoffs cannot legally be distributed under the project's open-source license
questions.explanation: Automation closes the gap between intention and consistency.

questions.question: Which two forms does the packet ship in?
options: handoff.md rendered as a printable PDF and handoff.json compiled into one compressed archive file
handoff.md and handoff.json, both from the same source artifacts; JSON wins on divergence
An email sent to the next operator and a Slack message posted to the team channel
handoff.yaml for humans to read and handoff.toml for the next agent session to load
questions.explanation: Markdown for humans, JSON for the next agent; both come from the same generator.

questions.question: What does the open_risks field in a handoff packet answer, per the lesson?
options: What model was used to generate the handoff packet itself
What could bite next session, plus a severity for each
How long the previous session ran before handing off
Which reviewer signed off on the previous session's work
questions.explanation: The lesson's seven-field table lists open_risks as answering 'what could bite next session, with severity'.

questions.question: What does the lesson say the cleanup phase emits before a handoff can be written?
options: A signed approval token issued by the verification gate
A full diff of every touched file, attached to handoff.json
A rollback script the next session can run automatically
An empty clean_state.json list required before a packet
questions.explanation: The lesson says the cleanup phase emits a clean_state.json of blocking issues, and an empty list is the precondition the handoff generator asserts before it writes a packet.

questions.question: What does the lesson recommend trimming the feedback log to in the packet?
options: The first K entries only, since later entries matter less than how the run began
A random sample of N entries, so the packet stays representative without growing large
The last K entries plus every entry with a non-zero exit, so failures still survive
Only the single most recent entry, discarding every earlier command in the log
questions.explanation: Asymmetric trim: failures must survive; trivia at the tail is cheap to keep.

questions.question: Per the lesson's clean-state table, why does a stray branch block a handoff?
options: Stray branches make handoff.json fail its JSON Schema validation
Git refuses to generate a diff across more than one branch
The reviewer agent cannot read state from a non-default branch
The next session's first commit would land on the wrong branch
questions.explanation: The lesson's table says a wrong branch means the next session's first commit lands in the wrong place, so the check requires the expected branch with no detached HEAD or orphan branches.
